title: 🏛️ Exams 2011–2026 · writing prepared: advise, warn, set rules ⭐⭐⭐

questions.prompt: (Exam 2026, general) You are writing an article that warns readers against the dangers of online shopping. Which sentence is the clearest warning?

options.text: You mustn't give your card number to a website you don't know.
Many people give their card number to websites they don't know.
You can give your card number to any website you like.
You might lose money on a website you don't know.

questions.explanation: A warning tells readers what not to do, and "mustn't" + base verb forbids the dangerous action. One sentence only describes what many people do, another only says that something bad is possible, and "can" allows the very thing the article warns against.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2026, technical) Task: "Your classmates believe the Internet is only for playing games, but you think it offers much more. Write an 8-line article for your school magazine in which you advise them on how to use the Internet as a tool for learning and improving their studies." What exactly must the article do?

options.text: Tell your classmates the story of the day you first played an online game.
Describe your favourite video game to your classmates in detail.
Warn your classmates against the dangers of spending long hours online.
Give your classmates advice on using the Internet to study better.

questions.explanation: The verb of the task is "advise": the article must tell classmates what is a good thing to do with the Internet, here to learn and improve their studies. Telling a story would be a narrative, describing a game would be a description, and warning against dangers would turn the advice upside down.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2016, technical) Task: "While working in a carpentry workshop at your technical school, one of your classmates had a small accident and cut his finger. You have decided to write an article for your school magazine to show how sorry you are and to give your schoolmates some advice on how to keep safe." Which sentence shows that the writer is sorry about the accident?

options.text: Our classmate cut his finger with a saw in the workshop.
You should always wear gloves when you use a saw.
I am so sorry that our classmate had this accident.
I hope our classmate will come back to school soon.

questions.explanation: The word "sorry" expresses regret: I am so sorry that + clause. One sentence only reports the facts, another gives advice (the second part of the task) and the sentence with "hope" expresses a wish, not regret.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2011, technical) Your leaflet on keeping the workshop tidy and safe needs one rule that sets an obligation, not a ban and not a piece of advice. Which line is it?

options.text: You mustn't wear loose clothes near the machines.
You shouldn't leave your bag on the table.
You must wear protective clothes at work.
Don't touch the saw with wet hands.

questions.explanation: Must + base verb sets an obligation: protective clothes are necessary, the workers have no choice. "Mustn't" and "Don't" forbid something, and "shouldn't" only gives advice against something.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2026, general) Task: "An increasing number of people rely on online shopping to make their lives easier. Write a 10-line article for a local magazine to warn them against the possible dangers of online shopping. State at least 3 sound arguments." Which of these points are sound arguments for the article?

options.text: You can compare prices from many shops without leaving your home.
Your bank card details can be stolen if the website is not secure.
Many shops in the town centre are closed on Sundays and holidays.
Some sellers keep your money and never send the goods.
Some websites sell fake products that break after a few days.
It is easy to spend too much because everything is one click away.

questions.explanation: The article must warn, so a sound argument names a real danger of buying online: stolen card details, goods paid for but never sent, fake products and overspending. Comparing prices is an advantage, and the Sunday closing of shops is off the topic: neither warns anyone of a danger.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2024, general) Task: "As a member of Go Green association, write a 10-line post to be shared on the association's Facebook page. Suggest at least three ways to reduce pollution and protect the environment." Put the parts of a good post in the best order.

options.text: Say that waste is increasing in town and harms the environment and people's health.
Ask the readers to act today and to share the post.
Greet the readers and say who is writing: the Go Green association.
Suggest three ways to reduce pollution, for example recycling, saving energy and walking.

questions.explanation: A post starts by greeting the readers and saying who writes. Then it explains the problem, because readers need a reason to act. Only then do the three ways to reduce pollution make sense. The post ends with a call to act today, which closes the message.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2022, technical) Task: "Write an eight-line post for your facebook page in which you talk about the negative effects of internet addiction and give some advice on how to use the internet safely." Which sentence gives advice AND supports it with a reason?

options.text: Some students miss important classes because they chat online for long hours every night.
You should log off at night because tired students study badly.
You should use the Internet less.
Internet addiction is a serious problem, so many worried parents ask their children to stop.

questions.explanation: The sentence with "should" and "because" gives advice (should + base verb) and its reason: tired students study badly. One sentence has "because" but only describes what some students do. Another gives advice without any reason. Another describes a problem and its result and gives no advice to the reader.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2019, general) Task: "Write a 10-line article for your school magazine in which you tell other students about the health risks of eating fast food and ways of avoiding this bad habit." Match each health risk with the best way of avoiding it.

options.text: Gaining too much weight
Tooth decay
Heart problems
Feeling tired in class
Eat less fat to keep your blood vessels clear.
Drink water instead of sugary drinks and brush your teeth after meals.
Go to bed early and eat breakfast to have energy in the morning.
Play sport or walk every day to burn calories.

questions.explanation: Each way names what it protects. Burning calories with sport or walking stops people gaining too much weight. Water instead of sugary drinks and brushing protect the teeth. Clear blood vessels look after the heart, so less fat goes with heart problems. An early bedtime and a good breakfast give energy and fight tiredness in class.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2016, technical) After a classmate cut his finger in the carpentry workshop, you give your schoolmates some advice on how to keep safe. Which piece of advice fits the article?

options.text: You should keep your fingers away from the blade.
You should buy a bigger saw for the whole workshop.
You might keep your fingers away from the blade.
You mustn't tell the teacher about an accident.

questions.explanation: The task asks for advice on keeping safe, so should + base verb and a safety tip: keep your fingers away from the blade. A bigger saw does not keep anyone safe, "might" only says that something is possible instead of advising, and hiding an accident from the teacher is the opposite of safe.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2011, technical) Task: "Your teacher has asked you to write a leaflet where you set rules on how to keep your work place tidy and safe." Which line is a correctly written rule for the leaflet?

options.text: You mustn't leave the machines on when nobody is working.
Don't leaving the machines on when nobody is working.
You must to switch off the machines when nobody is working.
You mustn't leaves the machines on when nobody is working.

questions.explanation: A rule can use mustn't + base verb, or Don't + base verb. "Don't leaving" and "mustn't leaves" put an ending on the verb that follows, and "must to" adds a "to" after the modal. Only "You mustn't leave the machines on…" is well formed.
